lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 130: Alt+Page Up and Down drop the selection on the neighbouring tab.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request one thirty: Alt Page Up and Alt Page Down drop the selection on the neighbouring tab.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
You press Alt+Page Down for the next tab, or Alt+Page Up for the previous one, with focus in the file view.
lines.say: You press Alt Page Down for the next tab, or Alt Page Up for the previous one, with focus in the file view.

lines.caption: A new function finds the tab one over, crossing the split, and never wrapping around.
Insert's file-list helper, now given that tab, picks the files to send and skips any already there.
Then Insert's shared drop moves or copies them, and focus stays on the tab you started from.
Both actions are in the Edit menu too, greyed out when nothing would move.
Insert itself now picks the other pane, then runs the same two steps as before.
Insert already sent files to the other pane; now two keys send them to the tab next door, without a drag.
The new keys have no transfer of their own: Insert's helpers now take the target tab, so all share one path.
In a text field, such as the location bar or a rename entry, nothing moves and the key goes on.
The lookup adds or subtracts one from the tab's position; in split view it steps into the other pane.
The target folder must be loaded and writable, and a tab showing the same folder gets nothing.
The drop rule moves on the same filesystem, copies across, and always moves into the Trash.
The menu items sit right after Drop on Other Pane, and both keys can be rebound like any action.
Insert behaves as before; the new text-field check never stops it, because a text field uses Insert itself.
In the test, the left pane holds alpha and beta, and the right pane holds gamma and delta.
Next goes alpha, beta, gamma, delta, crossing the split from beta to gamma; previous goes back.
Past the first or last tab, the keys do nothing.
Without split view, the order is just the one pane's tabs, from left to right.
With a selection and focus in the file view, files go one tab over, across the split, but never past the ends.
In a text field, or with a same, read-only or unloaded target folder, nothing moves.
A tab showing the Trash gets the files moved into the Trash.
Each of the three actions is now one line: pick a target tab, then hand it to the shared drop.
The PR changes the window's code and header, and adds its test, this page and its narration.
To undo it, revert this PR; it stores no setting.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It reuses Insert's code, mirrors the tab-switching keys, and finds tabs the way tab switching does.
In this session it built in the cloud container, with no warnings in the changed files, before the review fix.
The new test moved a file from beta to gamma with Alt+Page Down, and back with Alt+Page Up.
lines.say: The new test moved a file from beta to gamma with Alt Page Down, and back with Alt Page Up.

lines.caption: Nothing moved at the first or last tab or from the location bar; without split view a file moved once, then no further.
The Insert and drag tests still passed, and all 25 tests passed on that build, before CI's test fixes.
lines.say: The Insert and drag tests still passed, and all twenty-five tests passed on that build, before C I's test fixes.

lines.caption: A new rename step failed on the build without the fix, and passed with it, along with all 7 pairs.
lines.say: A new rename step failed on the build without the fix, and passed with it, along with all seven pairs.

lines.caption: Not run: the screenshot audit, and the same-folder, unloaded-tab and Trash cases.
Before the first push, a fresh agent reviewed the branch at level high: two findings, one fixed, one skipped.
The fix: during an inline rename, the keys would have moved the file being renamed; text fields now block them, and a test checks it.
The skipped finding was the missing explainer, which is this page.
CI's first review, at level high, found three small problems, R1 to R3, all in the test and all fixed.
lines.say: C I's first review, at level high, found three small problems, R one to R three, all in the test and all fixed.

lines.caption: R1: the rename check had no test; a new rename step now presses the key while renaming, and nothing moves.
lines.say: R one: the rename check had no test; a new rename step now presses the key while renaming, and nothing moves.

lines.caption: R2: the no-split step now proves there is no split, by checking the last tab; R3 removed comments the rules forbid.
lines.say: R two: the no-split step now proves there is no split, by checking the last tab; R three removed comments the rules forbid.

lines.caption: CI's second review found R1 to R3 resolved and raised three more low findings: one fixed by CI, two accepted.
lines.say: C I's second review found R one to R three resolved and raised three more low findings: one fixed by C I, two accepted.

lines.caption: R4: two settings lines in the test did nothing, so CI removed them; the last-tab check alone proves there's no split.
lines.say: R four: two settings lines in the test did nothing, so C I removed them; the last-tab check alone proves there's no split.

lines.caption: Accepted: R5, as F2 in the details view opens the in-place entry, and R6, as the next step reselects before acting.
lines.say: Accepted: R five, as F two in the details view opens the in-place entry, and R six, as the next step reselects before acting.

lines.caption: CI builds the packages and runs all 25 tests on this push, and its screenshots are audited after that run.
lines.say: C I builds the packages and runs all twenty-five tests on this push, and its screenshots are audited after that run.

lines.caption: Whether other desktops grab these keys, and the unloaded-tab and Trash cases, wait until after the merge.
The PR, the issue, the branch and CI's comments are linked here.
Part 3. Nothing depends on issue 128.
lines.say: Part 3. Nothing depends on issue one twenty-eight.

lines.caption: Dropping on a tab by number, or always copy and always move keys, are only ideas, with no issue yet.
In short: Alt+Page Up and Down now send the selection to the tab next door, just as a drop would.
lines.say: In short: Alt Page Up and Alt Page Down now send the selection to the tab next door, just as a drop would.
